rep_att_a#1.killer: fines increment outside the silt-curtain cell in the closed ~160k m³ under-ice water after 1 day
rep_att_a#1.why: Water under the ice has no outflow, so even a 95%-efficient cell leaves ~170 mg/L/day against a 0.25 mg/L limit, and the chain gain is only 1.17x.
rep_att_a#1.screen: 7 turbidity: 0.00013 (0.0015 even at 95% curtain efficiency); 2 ice bearing (25 t parked at moon-pool edge on 1.1 m ice): 0.39; 1 season window (1.1 m ice comes ~36 d after mid-Dec at snow-covered alpha 0.020, not 0.027): 0.75; 6 moon-pool heat (2 kW vs 0.8-1.5 kW loss): 1.4; 9 baseline: ratio 1.17

rep_att_b#4.killer: water depth at the village berth for a 2,000 t barge (80x15 m) carrying 1,780 t coal + ~100 t plant (draught 2.17 m)
rep_att_b#4.why: The ~1.5x saving on winter power is real, but a loaded hull draws more than Arctic village berths offer (it fits only deep Lena-type reaches), and a 2x Far-North capex premium wipes out the gain.
rep_att_b#4.screen: 3/11 wintering depth for loaded hull: 0.78 (Yana/Indigirka 0.58; Lena main stem 1.13); 6 moat heat (104 kW vs 69 kW for 0.5 m moat at -38.6 °C, 5 m/s): 1.5; 11 hull rise 1.29 m, uplift 76 kN/m vs 31 kN/m ice edge: 0.40 only if the moat is lost while burning; 8 heat-led market (1.57 MW reject heat vs village base load): >=1; 9 baseline: ratio 1.51 (0.89 at 2x Far-North capex)

rep_att_b#1.killer: fines from tailings returned down caved holes that connect to the lake bed (30 m³/h drawn, 1.9 t/m³, 20% fines, 0.5% escape = 1.37 t/day per module)
rep_att_b#1.why: The chain gain is genuine (~1.9x), but each module breaks the fishery limit in the closed under-ice lake within hours unless escape stays below ~0.1%, and parked modules at the hole edge are also short of capacity (0.80).

rep_att_b#2.killer: face-average heat-transfer coefficient needed to advance a 3 m adit 3.7-8 m/h with 6 °C water (E = 99 MJ/m³, 30% ice at -4 °C)
rep_att_b#2.why: The plan treats a stagnation-point heat-transfer value as the face average, so the face takes ~1/5 of the needed flux and advance drops ~5x (or the water thaws the roof instead), and even the claimed costs give only 1.35x on the chain.

rep_att_a#3.killer: coal demand within 150 km needed to absorb one rig's 80 kt/yr
rep_att_a#3.why: The repair gets to 1,800 rub/t only by selling 80 kt/yr, about 5x what villages within 150 km burn, and at a market-sized ~20 kt the idea's own 4,100 rub/t loses to the bank pit (0.87x).

rep_att_b#3.killer: river flow needed to dilute coal fines returned overboard with the dewatering-screen water (55 t/h; 5% <63 µm all escape + 0.5% of 10% fines at the cutter = 0.77 kg/s)
rep_att_b#3.why: An in-river cutter feeding an on-barge screen sends every sub-screen coal fine back with the slurry water, needing ~10x the flow available at the control section, although the 1.5x economics would have passed.
rep_att_b#3.screen: 7 turbidity: 0.09 at a 500 m control section (1.0 only with full mixing into the whole Kolyma mean flow; cutter alone 9.5); 1 season window (4 bends x 8-25 d + transit in 61 d of Jun-Jul): 0.82 (0.56-1.5); 8 market (4 x 10 kt clusters): OK; 9 baseline: ratio 1.52

rep_att_a#2.killer: thaw advance of a 2 m drift face (45 m drift within 30 d of a 90-d water season)
rep_att_a#2.why: The roof caves at about the right time only with central strength values, the drift face thaws at about half the rate a season needs, the water budget is short (0.58), and the chain gain is only 1.35x.
